mainTopic: Finishing the בכור discussion, then the ברייתא on ניסן as ראש השנה for months, leap years, and the שקלים, with their sources and laws
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier discussion about the year for giving a בכור to the כהן. Counting from birth applies to a בעל מום that we know was carried full term. Next comes a ברייתא: the first of ניסן is ראש השנה for months, for leap years, and for the שקלים collection. The גמרא looks for a source that ניסן is the first month. Proofs from the תורה, based on ripening and gathering, are rejected because the פסוקים never say 'most'. Instead, רבינא and other אמוראים prove it from נביאים and כתובים, which name each month with its number. ניסן as the 'new year for leap years' turns out to mean the deadline for declaring one, and the גמרא explains the dispute over whether that deadline is פורים or the end of אדר. For the שקלים, רבי יאשיה learns from a פסוק and a גזירה שווה that offerings come from a new collection starting in ניסן. שמואל adds that old funds are still valid, and a ברייתא says a private donor may give communal offerings if he hands them to the community. The amud ends in the middle of the גמרא's answer to why that last point needed to be said.

steps.title: Counting from birth applies to a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the earlier contradiction about when to start counting a בכור's year: the statement that counts from birth is about a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement is talking about a blemished animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves a contradiction from the previous discussion. The opinion that counts a בכור's year from its birth is talking about a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two statements seemed to clash about when the one-year deadline for giving a בכור to the כהן begins. A blemished בכור cannot be brought as a קרבן, so it is ready to be given to the כהן and eaten right away. That is why its year can start at birth. An unblemished one must wait until it is fit to be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: This one (points to one of the two statements being compared)
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be offered as a קרבן
Firstborn male animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: That one is about a blemished animal.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the earlier statement that counts the בכור's year from the day it was born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised just before this section (on the previous daf) about when a בכור's year begins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement refers to a different kind of animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to talk about the same kind of בכור and to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting from birth applies to a בעל מום, which can be eaten right away. Counting from when it is fit applies to an unblemished animal.

steps.title: Can a blemished newborn really be eaten right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: even a blemished newborn should not be eaten on the day it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a blemished animal be eaten right away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It asks how a newborn בעל מום could be eaten on the day it is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn animal normally has to wait eight days, because maybe it was born too early and will not survive. If so, even a blemished בכור is not ready on its birth day. Then the claim that its year starts from birth seems hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? Can it really? (a challenging question)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a בעל מום may ever be eaten; it may. The question is only whether it may be eaten immediately on the day of birth.

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל מוּם מִי מָצֵי אָכֵיל לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: A blemished animal — can one eat it?
phrases.notes: He means right away on the day it's born, since newborns usually wait eight days in case they were born too early.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם מִי מָצֵי אָכֵיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that a blemished בכור is ready to eat from birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A newborn may not be eaten until it is eight days old, so even a בעל מום is not ready on its birth day.

steps.title: When we know the pregnancy was full term
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where we know for sure the animal finished its full months in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he knows for sure that the animal's months were completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. It explains that the case is one where we know for certain the animal was carried full term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight-day wait exists only because of the doubt that the animal may have been born early. If we know when it was conceived and that the full pregnancy was completed, there is no doubt. Then a blemished בכור may be eaten on the day it is born, so its year really can start from birth.
steps.whatToRemember: Counting from birth applies to a בעל מום where we know it was full term. Then it is ready to be eaten on its birth day, and the year starts at birth.

phrases.english: Where he knows for certain about it
that its months were completed.
phrases.notes: This means the full pregnancy was finished, so there's no worry it was born too early.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקִים לֵיהּ בֵּיהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: it is limited to an animal known to be full term.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every newborn must wait eight days, so a blemished בכור could not be eaten from birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the pregnancy is known to have been complete, there is no need to wait, so the animal may be eaten from birth.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists what the first of ניסן is the new year for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the first of ניסן is ראש השנה for months, for leap years, and for the שקלים collection. Some add the renting of houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: On the first of ניסן is the new year for months, for leap years, and for the collection of the שקלים. Some say: also for renting houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It brings a ברייתא that adds more items for which the first of ניסן is the start of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed only kings and festivals for the first of ניסן. This ברייתא adds three more: counting the months, עיבורין (leap years), and the new collection of שקלים for the בית המקדש. A further opinion, יש אומרים, adds house rentals. The גמרא will now try to find a source for each item, starting with months.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years, when an extra month is added
Taking the half-שקל funds to buy communal קרבנות

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets the plan for the coming discussion. The גמרא will go through it item by item and ask for a source for each.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On the first of Nisan is the new year for months,
phrases.notes: 'For months' means Nisan counts as month number one when numbering the months.

phrases.english: and for leap years, and for the collection of the shekels.
And some say: also for the renting of houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָחֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section; it leaves the בכור discussion and expands on the משנה's list for ניסן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first of ניסן starts the year for months, leap years, and the שקלים collection. Some add house rentals.

steps.title: What is the source for counting months from ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that ניסן is the new year for months.
steps.simpleTranslation: For months, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's first item, months. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated a rule without a source. Now the גמרא goes back to the first item and asks where the תורה teaches that ניסן is the first month.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: For months, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the first item listed in the ברייתא of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ניסן is the first month for counting months.

steps.title: The פסוק in שמות: the month of the פסח lamb is the first month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמות 12, which calls a certain month 'the first of the months' and describes the פסח lamb being taken and slaughtered in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'This month shall be for you the head of months; it is the first for you of the months of the year. Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb for his father's house, a lamb for a household. And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month, and they shall slaughter it, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first half of its proof. The תורה calls 'this month' the first month, and that month is the one in which the קרבן פסח is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק does not name the month. It only says the first month is the month of the קרבן פסח, from the 10th to the 14th. The גמרא still needs a second פסוק to show which calendar month that is.
steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק by itself does not mention ניסן. Its job is to link 'the first month' to 'the month of פסח'. The next step identifies that month as ניסן.

phrases.english: As it is written: "This month shall be for you the head of months;
phrases.notes: שמות 12:2–6

phrases.english: it is the first for you of the months of the year.

phrases.aramaic: דַּבְּרוּ אֶל כׇּל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר
phrases.english: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying:
On the tenth of this month

phrases.aramaic: וְיִקְחוּ לָהֶם אִישׁ שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבוֹת
phrases.english: they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb for his father's house,
a lamb for a household.
And it shall be kept by you

phrases.aramaic: עַד אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה
phrases.english: until the fourteenth day of this month,
and they shall slaughter it, etc."
phrases.notes: The point of quoting this far is to show that 'this first month' is the month of the קרבן פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the month of the קרבן פסח is called the first month.

steps.title: The month of ripening is ניסן, so ניסן is the first month
steps.stepSummary: Using דברים 16:1, which places פסח in the month of ripening, the גמרא shows that the month is ניסן. ניסן is therefore called 'first'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'Keep the month of ripening.' Which month has ripening in it? You must say this is ניסן, and the תורה calls it first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the פסח month, which the תורה called 'first', is the month of ripening, and that month is ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק says פסח must fall in חודש האביב, the month when the grain ripens. The only month that fits is ניסן. Put together with the פסוק in שמות, the month the תורה calls 'first' is ניסן, so the months are counted from ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (the only possible answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The first proof joins two פסוקים: the פסח month is called 'first' (שמות 12), and the פסח month is the month of ripening (דברים 16). The next steps test whether 'ripening' really points only to ניסן, and step 12 shows it does not.

phrases.english: And it is written: "Keep the month of ripening,"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:1. The פסוק continues 'and make the פסח', which links this month to פסח.

phrases.english: Which is the month that has ripening in it?
You must say: this is Nisan,
and it calls it 'first'.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the פסוק in שמות, which called this month the first month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 6 by identifying the פסח month as ניסן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This proof claims ניסן is the month the תורה calls 'first'; the גמרא goes on to reject it in step 12.

steps.title: Maybe the month is אייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from the previous step. Maybe the 'first month' with פסח is אייר, not ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is אייר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the last proof. Maybe the 'month of ripening' where פסח falls is actually אייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the first month is ניסן because פסח must be in the month of ripening. The גמרא now asks how we know ripening points to ניסן and not to the month after it.

phrases.english: But say it is Iyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the month in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'month of ripening' means ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another month could also fit the description

steps.title: אייר has no ripening
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the month must be one of ripening, and in אייר the grain has already ripened.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need a month of ripening, and there isn't any in אייר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers quickly that אייר does not fit. By then the ripening is already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires a month in which grain is ripening. In אייר the grain is already ripe, so the description does not match.

phrases.english: We need ripening, and there is none.
phrases.notes: In אייר the grain has already ripened, so it isn't a month of ripening anymore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אייר challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אייר might be the month of ripening
steps.terutzMaskana: אייר has no ripening, so it is ruled out

steps.title: Maybe the month is אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the month before ניסן. Some grain begins to ripen in אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is אדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other direction. Maybe the month of ripening is אדר, when some grain already starts ripening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אייר was too late, so the גמרא checks whether a month that is too early could also fit. If אדר works, the proof for ניסן falls apart.

phrases.english: But say it is Adar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same proof
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'month of ripening' means ניסן

steps.title: We need most of the ripening
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the month must hold most of the ripening, and that happens in ניסן, not אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need most of the ripening, and that isn't in אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a little ripening is not enough. The month has to be the one where most of the ripening happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer adds a new requirement: 'most' of the ripening. With that requirement, אדר drops out and only ניסן is left.

phrases.english: We need most of the ripening, and there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אדר challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a qualifier to the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ripening is enough, so אדר could fit
steps.terutzMaskana: The month must have most of the ripening, which is ניסן

steps.title: The verse never says most
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. The פסוק only says 'ripening', not 'most of the ripening'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'most of the ripening' written in the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down its own answer. The word 'most' is not in the פסוק, so אדר is still possible and the proof from פסח fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 11 depended on reading 'most' into the פסוק. Since the פסוק only says 'ripening', אדר is still possible. That is why the גמרא now needs a new source.

phrases.english: Is "most of the ripening" written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 11, which brings down the proof of step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the month of ripening
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'most' is not in the פסוק

steps.title: רב חסדא proves it from סוכות in the seventh month
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a new proof. The month of gathering is תשרי, and the Torah calls it 'seventh', so ניסן is first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: we learn it from here. 'But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather the produce of the land.' Which month has gathering? You must say it is תשרי, and the Torah calls it 'seventh'.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the proof from פסח failed, רב חסדא brings a proof from סוכות. The Torah calls the month of gathering, תשרי, the 'seventh' month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשרי is the seventh month, then counting back six months makes ניסן the first. The proof now depends on the month of gathering being תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: The fall month of ראש השנה and סוכות

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said, from here:
"But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:39

phrases.english: when you gather in the produce of the land,"
Which month has gathering in it?
You must say: this is Tishrei,
and it calls it "seventh."
phrases.notes: If תשרי is seventh, count back and ניסן comes out first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new one
steps.raayaObject: ניסן is the first of the months
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 23:39, where the month of gathering, תשרי, is called seventh

steps.title: Maybe it is מרחשון, seventh from אייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. Maybe the 'seventh month' is מרחשון, counted from אייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is מרחשון, and what does 'seventh' mean? Seventh from אייר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב חסדא's proof the same way it tested the first one. Maybe the month of gathering is מרחשון, which is seventh if you start counting from אייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the year started in אייר, then מרחשון would be the seventh month. The challenge uses a month that is one too late, just like the challenge of אייר in step 8.

phrases.english: But say it is Marcheshvan,
and what is "seventh"? Seventh from Iyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's proof
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the month of gathering is תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later month could be 'seventh' if the count starts at אייר

steps.title: מרחשון has no gathering
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the month must have gathering, and by מרחשון the gathering is already over.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need gathering, and there isn't any in מרחשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מרחשון does not fit. The crops have already been gathered by then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 9. A month that is too late has nothing left to gather, so it does not match the פסוק.

phrases.english: We need gathering, and there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מרחשון challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרחשון might be the month of gathering
steps.terutzMaskana: מרחשון has no gathering, so it is ruled out

steps.title: Maybe it is אלול, seventh from אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the month before תשרי. Maybe the 'seventh month' is אלול, counted from אדר, since gathering begins in אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is אלול, and what does 'seventh' mean? Seventh from אדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a month that is too early. Some gathering starts in אלול, and it would be seventh if you count from אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the challenge of אדר in step 10. If אלול fits, then the first month would be אדר and not ניסן.

phrases.english: But say it is Elul,
and what is "seventh"? Seventh from Adar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב חסדא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the month of gathering is תשרי

steps.title: We need most of the gathering
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the month must hold most of the gathering, and that happens in תשרי, not אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need most of the gathering, and that isn't in אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the month has to be the one where most of the gathering happens. That is תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move as step 11, adding the word 'most'. With that requirement, אלול is ruled out.

phrases.english: We need most of the gathering, and there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אלול challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a qualifier to the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gathering is enough, so אלול could fit
steps.terutzMaskana: The month must have most of the gathering, which is תשרי

steps.title: The verse never says most gathering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this answer as well. The פסוק does not say 'most of the gathering', so רב חסדא's proof fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'most of the gathering' written in the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer, just as it did in step 12. Without the word 'most', אלול is still possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both Torah proofs have now failed for the same reason. Each one needed the word 'most', and that word is not in either פסוק. This sets up the move to a source outside the Torah.

phrases.english: Is "most of the gathering" written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 17, which brings down רב חסדא's proof
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'most' is not in the פסוק

steps.title: רבינא learns it from the נביאים: שבט is the eleventh month
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says this is not learned from the Torah but from דברי קבלה. זכריה calls שבט the eleventh month.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: we did not learn this from the Torah of משה רבינו. We learned it from the words of the Prophets: 'On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of שבט.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives up on finding it in the Torah. He brings a פסוק in נביאים that names the month outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זכריה names the month directly: the eleventh month is שבט. Counting back from שבט makes ניסן the first. Since the month is named, there is no room for the 'which month is it?' challenges.

keyTerms.meaning: The Five Books of the Torah
The books of נביאים and כתובים

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's hints about ניסן cannot rule out a neighboring month, so the clear source is a פסוק in the Prophets that names the month and its number.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule this basic can rest on the Prophets when the Torah's wording is not precise enough.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ,
phrases.english: this matter we did not learn from the Torah of Moshe our teacher;
we learned it from the words of tradition:
phrases.notes: This means the books of the Prophets and the Writings, not the Five Books.

phrases.english: "On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month,
phrases.notes: זכריה 1:7

phrases.english: which is the month of Shevat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא, דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed Torah proofs with a proof from נביאים
steps.raayaObject: ניסן is the first of the months
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 1:7, where שבט is called the eleventh month

steps.title: רבה בר עולא learns it from אסתר: טבת is the tenth month
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא brings another פסוק, from מגילת אסתר, which calls טבת the tenth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said, from here: 'And אסתר was taken to King אחשורוש, to his royal house, in the tenth month, which is the month of טבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא gives a second proof from outside the Torah. אסתר calls טבת the tenth month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טבת is the tenth month, counting back makes ניסן the first. Like רבינא's proof, it names the month directly, so it cannot be pushed back like the Torah proofs.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said, from here:
"And Esther was taken to King Achashverosh
phrases.notes: אסתר 2:16

phrases.english: to his royal house
in the tenth month, which is the month of Teves."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proof from מגילת אסתר, a book of כתובים (רבינא's proof came from זכריה, in נביאים)
steps.raayaObject: ניסן is the first of the months
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 2:16, where טבת is called the tenth month

steps.title: רב כהנא's proof from זכריה: כסלו is the ninth month
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא proves from a פסוק in זכריה that months are counted from ניסן, because כסלו is called the ninth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: We learn it from here: 'On the fourth day of the ninth month, in כסלו.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adds one more proof that the months are counted from ניסן. A נביא calls כסלו 'the ninth month'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you count from ניסן, כסלו really is the ninth month: ניסן, אייר, סיון, תמוז, אב, אלול, תשרי, חשון, כסלו. Like רבינא's proof in step 19, this comes from דברי קבלה, the books of the נביאים, and not from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of כסלו, the ninth month counting from ניסן

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: from here:
"On the fourth of the ninth month, in Kislev."
phrases.notes: זכריה 7:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proof that joins רבינא and רבה בר עולא in using פסוקים from נביאים and כתובים.
steps.raayaObject: That the months are numbered starting from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 7:1, which calls כסלו the ninth month

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב's proof from אסתר: סיון is the third month
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a פסוק from מגילת אסתר that calls סיון the third month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We learn it from here: 'And the king's scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of סיון.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא brings another פסוק. This one calls סיון 'the third month'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting from ניסן, סיון is third: ניסן, אייר, סיון. This proof comes from מגילת אסתר, like רבה בר עולא's proof in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of סיון, the third month

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ya'akov said: from here:
"And the king's scribes were called at that time,
in the third month, which is the month of Sivan."
phrases.notes: אסתר 8:9

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another parallel proof for the same point.
steps.raayaObject: That the months are numbered starting from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 8:9, which calls סיון the third month

steps.title: רב אשי's proof from אסתר: אדר is the twelfth month
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings the פסוק about המן's lottery, which calls אדר the twelfth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We learn it from here: 'He cast a פור, which is the lot, before המן, from day to day and from month to month, to the twelfth month, which is the month of אדר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a פסוק from the story of פורים that calls אדר 'the twelfth month'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדר can only be the twelfth month if the count starts at ניסן. Each אמורא is simply choosing a different פסוק to prove the same point.

keyTerms.meaning: A lot, the lottery המן cast
A lot (the Hebrew word for פור)
The month of אדר, the twelfth month

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: from here:
"He cast pur, which is the lot, before Haman
from day to day and from month to month,
to the twelfth, which is the month of Adar."
phrases.notes: אסתר 3:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another parallel proof for the same point.
steps.raayaObject: That the months are numbered starting from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 3:7, which calls אדר the twelfth month

steps.title: The clearest proof: 'The first month, which is ניסן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers the most direct פסוק of all, which openly calls ניסן the first month.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that we learn it from here: 'In the first month, which is the month of ניסן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an even simpler proof: a פסוק that says outright that ניסן is the first month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק seems best of all, because it names ניסן as 'first' with no need to count. That makes the next question obvious: why didn't everyone just use it?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (an extra option)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: from here:
"In the first month, which is the month of Nisan."
phrases.notes: אסתר 3:7, the start of the same פסוק רב אשי just used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A final, more direct proof, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.raayaObject: That ניסן is the first of the months
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 3:7, 'the first month, which is ניסן'

steps.title: Why didn't everyone use the clearest verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all the other אמוראים did not use the פסוק that openly calls ניסן the first month.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them, what is the reason they did not say it from this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the other אמוראים skipped the clearest פסוק. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פסוק says outright 'the first month is ניסן', bringing a less direct פסוק looks unnecessary. So there must be some weakness in the clear-looking פסוק.

phrases.english: And all of them, what is the reason
that they did not say it from this one?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the פסוק from step 24, 'the first month, which is ניסן'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the earlier proofs were needed, given the clear פסוק in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the other אמוראים chose less direct פסוקים instead of the clearest one

steps.title: 'First' may only mean first in that story
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that 'first' in that פסוק could mean first in relation to the story of המן's decree, not first of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps what does 'first' mean? First for its own matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the clear-looking פסוק is not a real proof. 'First' might only mean first in the story being told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מגילת אסתר, ניסן could be called 'first' because it was the first month of המן's lottery, not because it opens the year. Numbers like 'ninth' or 'twelfth' cannot be explained away like that, so those פסוקים prove more.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own matter, in its own context

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the clearest-sounding פסוק is always the strongest proof. Here the plain word 'first' turns out weaker than a number like 'twelfth', because 'first' can have a local meaning.

phrases.english: Perhaps, what does "first" mean?
First for its own matter.
phrases.notes: He means the first month of the story of המן's decree, not the first month of the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'first' could mean first within the story of the decree, so the פסוק does not prove that the year's months start from ניסן.

steps.title: Why our משנה does not list ניסן as new year for months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that our משנה leaves out 'ניסן is the new year for months' because it only deals with years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא of our משנה? He is dealing with years. He is not dealing with months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks, in very few words, why our משנה did not mention months the way the ברייתא did, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ניסן as the new year for months, but our משנה does not. The answer is that our משנה only lists 'new years' for counting years, such as kings and festivals. The order of the months is a different topic, so it is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: He is dealing with, talking about

steps.whatToRemember: The months are numbered from ניסן, proven from פסוקים in נביאים and כתובים. Our משנה leaves this out only because it deals with years, not months.

phrases.english: And our tanna?
phrases.notes: Why didn't our משנה list ניסן as the new year for months, like the ברייתא did?

phrases.english: He is dealing with years;
he is not dealing with months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having proven ניסן is the new year for months, the גמרא explains why our משנה does not say so.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה only deals with counting years, so the order of months is outside its subject.

steps.title: Do we really count leap years from ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the ברייתא's next phrase, 'for leap years', and challenges it: is a leap year really counted from ניסן?
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'for leap years'. Do we count leap years from ניסן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the ברייתא's words 'for leap years' and asks whether ניסן really starts the count for leap years. The proof for this challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said ניסן is the new year for עיבורין, adding a month to make a leap year. The גמרא doubts this and is about to bring a ברייתא that seems to tie leap years to תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years, adding an extra month to the year

phrases.english: "And for leap years":
Do we count leap years from Nisan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the topic of months to the next item in the ברייתא, leap years.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that ניסן is the new year for leap years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leap years seem to be connected to תשרי, not ניסן, as the next ברייתא will show.

steps.title: A ברייתא: leap years are declared only after ראש השנה, and only אדר is added
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. A leap year may not be declared before ראש השנה, may be declared right after it if needed, and the added month is always אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: We do not make the year a leap year before ראש השנה, and if they did, it is not a leap year. But under pressure, we may make it a leap year right after ראש השנה. And even so, the only month added is אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show why it doubts that leap years are counted from ניסן. Step 30 answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes ראש השנה in תשרי the earliest point for declaring a leap year, which makes it look like leap years are tied to תשרי. It also says the extra month is always a second אדר, so it is unclear in what way ניסן is the 'new year' for leap years.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a leap year, add a month
A leap year, a year with an extra month

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין הַשָּׁנָה לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: We do not make the year a leap year before Rosh HaShana,
and if they made it a leap year, it is not a leap year.
But because of pressing need,

phrases.aramaic: מְעַבְּרִין אוֹתָהּ אַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִיָּד.
phrases.english: we make it a leap year immediately after Rosh HaShana.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵּן, אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶלָּא אֲדָר.
phrases.english: And even so, we add only Adar.
phrases.notes: Even when they declare it early, the extra month is a second אדר, added at the end of the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין הַשָּׁנָה לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge of step 28.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that leap years are not counted from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: no leap year may be declared before ראש השנה, it may be declared right after it under pressure, and only אדר is ever added

steps.title: Leap years means the cutoff for declaring them
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'new year for leap years' means ניסן is the deadline after which a leap year can no longer be declared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'leap years' mean here? It means the stopping point for leap years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 28-29. ניסן is not where leap years start; it is where the chance to declare one ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed 'new year for leap years' meant the starting point for declaring one, but the ברייתא in step 29 showed declarations can begin right after ראש השנה in תשרי. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the ברייתא differently: ניסן marks the end. Once ניסן comes, the court can no longer turn the past year into a leap year.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years, years with an extra month added
The stopping point for declaring leap years
What is / what does it mean

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 29. Under pressing need, the court can already declare a leap year right after ראש השנה in תשרי; ניסן is only the point where the chance to declare one ends.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is meant by 'leap years'?
The stopping point of leap years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי עִיבּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 28 and backed up in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'New year for leap years' means ניסן is when leap-year declarations begin.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means ניסן is when the chance to declare a leap year ends.

steps.title: Proof that a leap year can be declared through all of אדר
steps.stepSummary: A משנה records testimony that a leap year may be declared all through אדר, against those who limited it to פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: They testified that a leap year may be declared all through אדר, because some had said: only until פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the deadline for declaring a leap year is the end of אדר, meaning the start of ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a leap year can be declared all through אדר, then the cutoff is when ניסן begins. That supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that ניסן is the end point. The משנה also shows there was an earlier view setting the cutoff at פורים, which the גמרא will now explain.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified (gave testimony about a rule)

phrases.english: As we learned: They testified
phrases.notes: 'They' are two Sages, רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס, whose testimony is recorded in that משנה.

phrases.english: that we may make the year a leap year all through אדר.
For there were those who said: only until פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הֵן הֵעִידוּ שֶׁמְּעַבְּרִין הַשָּׁנָה כׇּל אֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 30 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That ניסן is the cutoff for declaring a leap year.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה recording testimony that a leap year may be declared through all of אדר.

steps.title: Why limit leap years to פורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reason of the view that a leap year can only be declared until פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who said: only until פורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to understand the rejected view. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says some held 'until פורים' without giving a reason. Since the year's months are not over yet, it is not obvious why פורים should matter.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who said
until פורים?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד הַפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opposing view mentioned in the משנה of step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind setting the leap-year deadline at פורים.

steps.title: After פורים people start preparing for פסח
steps.stepSummary: Since people begin studying פסח laws thirty days before, on פורים, a late leap year might make them careless about חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said: We ask about the laws of פסח thirty days before פסח, people would come to treat חמץ lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'until פורים' view: from פורים on, people are already getting ready for פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after פורים, on the 15th of אדר, is thirty days before פסח, so everyone starts learning and preparing for פסח then. If the court then adds a month, פסח is pushed off, and people who already geared up may feel it isn't serious and get careless about חמץ when it finally comes.

keyTerms.meaning: To treat lightly, to be careless

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
We ask about the laws of פסח
thirty days before פסח,
people will come to treat חמץ lightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: שׁוֹאֲלִין בְּהִלְכוֹת הַפֶּסַח קוֹדֶם לַפֶּסַח שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Declaring a leap year after פורים, when פסח preparation has begun, could lead people to be careless about חמץ.

steps.title: The other view: people know leap years depend on calculation
steps.stepSummary: The Sages who allow declaring through all of אדר say people understand the court simply finished its calculations late.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view: It is well known that a leap year depends on calculation, and people will think: the calculation was only completed by the Sages just now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other Sages are not worried about a late leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that a leap year is decided by the court's calculations. So if it is declared after פורים, people will assume the Sages only now finished working it out, and will not lose respect for פסח or חמץ. That is why the deadline can be the end of אדר.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other view)

phrases.english: And the other view?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how the Sages who allow all of אדר answer this worry.

phrases.english: It is well known that a leap year
the matter depends on calculation,
and they will think: it is the calculation
that the Sages did not complete
until now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view's response to the worry in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People understand a late leap year as the result of late calculations, so they will not become careless about פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views on the leap-year deadline: until פורים (worry about carelessness with חמץ) or all of אדר (people know it depends on calculation). Either way, ניסן is the final cutoff.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave this out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה does not list ניסן as the new year for leap years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא? Why doesn't he mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to our משנה and asks why it skipped this point. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ניסן as the new year for leap years, and we now understand what that means. So why didn't our משנה include it in its list for ניסן too?

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, the author of our משנה

phrases.english: And our תנא?
phrases.notes: Why didn't our משנה list ניסן as the new year for leap years?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion to compare the ברייתא with our משנה, like step 27 did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why our משנה omits ניסן as the new year for leap years.

steps.title: Our משנה lists only beginnings, not endings
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה only lists dates where something begins; ניסן for leap years is an ending, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is dealing with beginnings; he is not dealing with endings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: our משנה only lists starting points, and ניסן for leap years is a stopping point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item in our משנה is a date that starts a new count. Since step 30 explained that ניסן for leap years is the END of the chance to declare one, it does not fit the משנה's list.
steps.whatToRemember: ניסן is the 'new year for leap years' only as a deadline. That is why the ברייתא mentions it but our משנה, which lists only beginnings, does not.

phrases.english: He is dealing with beginnings,
he is not dealing with endings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35 using the explanation from step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה only lists starting points; ניסן for leap years is an ending point.

steps.title: What is the source for the שקלים new year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא, that ניסן is the new year for the שקלים collection, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said ניסן is the new year for the collection of the שקלים. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא: ניסן begins the year for the שקלים. It asks where this comes from, setting up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every אדר the people gave a half-שקל, and this money bought the communal offerings. The question is why the new fund starts in ניסן and not some other month.

keyTerms.meaning: The collection taken from the half-שקל donations to pay for communal offerings
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And for the collection of the shekels.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new item in the ברייתא's list of new years.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that ניסן begins the year for the שקלים collection.

steps.title: Bring offerings from a new collection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה reads the פסוק about the monthly offering as an instruction to renew the fund and bring offerings from a new collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה said: the פסוק says, 'This is the burnt offering of each month in its month, for the months of the year.' The Torah is saying: renew, and bring the offering from a new collection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה gives the first half of the answer: the Torah wants communal offerings to come from a fresh, yearly collection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for the months of the year' look extra. רבי יאשיה reads 'חדשי' as related to 'חַדֵּשׁ', renew, so once a year the fund must be renewed. This step does not yet say which month; that comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya said: the verse says:
"This is the burnt offering of each month in its month
for the months of the year"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:14

phrases.english: The Torah is saying: renew
phrases.notes: He reads 'לחדשי', 'for the months', as if it says 'חַדֵּשׁ', 'make new'.

phrases.english: and bring an offering from a new collection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37, first part.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'for the months of the year' teaches that offerings must come from a renewed yearly collection.

steps.title: The word 'year' links it to ניסן
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שווה on the word 'year' shows that this renewed year begins in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learn 'year' from 'year' that it starts in ניסן, as it is written: 'It shall be the first of the months of the year for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by showing which month the new collection starts in: ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'year' appears in the פסוק about the monthly offering and in the פסוק about ניסן being first. A גזירה שווה connects them, so the 'year' of the offering fund starts in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one פסוק from another because they share the same word

phrases.english: And we learn "year" "year" from Nisan,
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שווה: the same word 'year' in two פסוקים links them together.

phrases.english: as it is written: "It is the first for you
of the months of the year."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation by identifying ניסן as the starting month.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שווה of 'year' and 'year' with the ניסן פסוק sets the start of the offering-fund year in ניסן.

steps.title: Why not learn from תשרי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the גזירה שווה is not made with a פסוק about תשרי, which also uses the word 'year'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'year' from 'year' from תשרי, as it is written: 'From the beginning of the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link to ניסן: there is also a פסוק about תשרי with the word 'year'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שווה works through a shared word, and 'year' appears for תשרי too. So why pick ניסן over תשרי?

keyTerms.meaning: But let us learn it instead
From the beginning of the year (a פסוק understood as referring to תשרי)

phrases.english: But let us learn "year" "year" from Tishrei,
as it is written: "From the beginning of the year"!
phrases.notes: דברים 11:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of ניסן in the גזירה שווה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שווה linking the offering 'year' to ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'year' also appears for תשרי, so the same method could point to תשרי instead.

steps.title: Match 'year with months' to 'year with months'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a 'year' mentioned together with months is learned from another 'year' mentioned with months, which fits ניסן, not תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn a 'year' that has 'months' with it from a 'year' that has 'months' with it. We do not learn a 'year' that has 'months' with it from a 'year' that has no 'months' with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ניסן link: the better match is the פסוק that, like ours, says 'months of the year'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the offering פסוק and the ניסן פסוק say 'לחדשי השנה', months of the year. The תשרי פסוק only says 'year' without months. A closer match wins.
steps.whatToRemember: ניסן starts the year for the שקלים because the offering פסוק and the ניסן פסוק both say 'months of the year', so they are linked by a גזירה שווה.

phrases.english: We learn a "year" that has "months" with it
from a "year" that has "months" with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין שָׁנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהּ חֳדָשִׁים
phrases.english: and we do not learn a "year" that has "months" with it
from a "year" that has no "months" with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Closer textual match: both פסוקים share the phrase 'months of the year'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any פסוק with the word 'year', including the תשרי one, could serve for the גזירה שווה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the ניסן פסוק, which mentions months like ours, is the proper match.

steps.title: New funds are best, old funds still work
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that communal offerings on ראש חודש ניסן should be bought from the new collection, but if bought from the old one they are valid, though the מצוה is lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: communal offerings brought on the first of ניסן should ideally be brought from the new funds. If he brought them from the old funds, he has fulfilled his obligation, but he missed the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: how strict is the rule of using the new collection? שמואל says it is the ideal way, but it does not stop the offering from counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 38–39 taught that the fund renews in ניסן. שמואל adds that this is a מצוה done the best way, not a condition for the offering to count. Old money still makes the offering valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings, brought for the whole nation
The new funds / the old funds
He missed the מצוה (the ideal way)

steps.confusionAlert: 'יצא' does not mean everything was perfect. The offering counts, but the ideal מצוה of using the new funds was missed.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Communal offerings that are brought on the first of Nisan —
it is a מצוה to bring them from the new funds.
And if he brought them from the old funds, he has fulfilled his obligation,
but he has missed the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule of a new collection by defining how binding it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the new funds on ראש חודש ניסן is the ideal מצוה; old funds still make the offering valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling as שמואל, word for word.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: communal offerings brought on the first of ניסן should ideally be brought from the new funds. If he brought them from the old funds, he has fulfilled his obligation, but he missed the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what שמואל said, as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תניא נמי הכי' means a ברייתא agrees with the statement just made. This shows שמואל's ruling matches an earlier teaching of the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Communal offerings that are brought on the first of Nisan —
it is a מצוה to bring them from the new funds,
and if he brought them from the old funds, he has fulfilled his obligation,
but he has missed the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that old funds are valid but miss the מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: A private donor may give communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that if a private person donates communal offerings from his own money, they are valid, as long as he hands them over to the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if an individual donated them from his own money, they are valid, as long as he hands them over to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds a new case: a private person paying for the communal offerings himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally communal offerings come from the public fund. The ברייתא allows a private donation, but only if he gives full ownership to the community, so it truly becomes a communal offering.

keyTerms.meaning: That he hands them over to the community

steps.whatToRemember: New שקלים funds are the ideal for ראש חודש ניסן offerings; old funds or a private donation (handed to the community) still work.

phrases.english: And an individual who donated them from his own money, they are valid,
as long as he hands them over to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with an added case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Privately donated communal offerings are valid if ownership is given to the community.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to teach that a private person's donated communal offerings are valid if he hands them over to the community. It seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last ruling of the ברייתא from step 44. If a person gives his own animal to the community and hands it over properly, of course it counts as a communal offering. So why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the classic 'פשיטא' challenge. The גמרא does not argue with the ruling. It asks why it needed to be written at all. The assumption is that a ברייתא does not waste words, so a ruling that seems obvious must be teaching something we would not have known.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! Used to ask why a source bothered to state something that seems self-understood.

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא does not mean the גמרא disagrees with the ruling. It agrees, and only asks why the ruling needed to be stated.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: What's obvious is the ruling from the ברייתא we just learned: someone may donate communal offerings if he hands them over to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling in step 44.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a private person may donate communal offerings if he hands them over to the community.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the animal is properly handed over to the community, it plainly belongs to the community. So the ruling seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: You might have worried that perhaps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. The ruling was needed because someone might have had a certain worry. The worry starts with 'perhaps', and the rest of it continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we should be concerned that perhaps…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to 'It is obvious!' by setting up a possible mistaken thought, a worry someone might have had. The sentence stops in the middle, so the actual worry comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהו דתימא' introduces a mistaken first thought (a הוה אמינא) that the ברייתא wanted to rule out. The word 'ליחוש' tells us the mistaken thought is a worry, a fear that something could go wrong. Because the ברייתא had to rule this worry out, its statement turns out not to be obvious after all.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces a mistaken idea the source wanted to rule out.
We should be concerned. Raises a worry.

phrases.english: Lest you say: we should be concerned that perhaps

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the פשיטא challenge of step 45.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed to rule out a mistaken worry (מהו דתימא, then the conclusion).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have been worried that something could go wrong with a private person's donation. The details continue in the next part of the text.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come: the ברייתא teaches that this worry is not a reason to disqualify the donation.
